title: Avoid Hidden Accessor Copies
subtitle: Can a harmless-looking getter dominate a hot-path hash operation?

metrics.label: CPU cycles
metrics.explanation: Cycles expose the repeated cost of constructing and destroying accessor results.

metrics.label: Instructions
metrics.explanation: The direct-member form removes copy-constructor instructions from every call.

metrics.label: IPC
metrics.explanation: IPC adds processor context; the primary claim is less work per call.

learning.change: The optimized method passes existing Location and State members instead of getters that return copies by value.
learning.hypothesis: Removing two temporaries from every hot-path call should reduce instructions and cycles while preserving the profile key.
learning.caution: The educational stand-ins make copy construction observable; absolute speedups are not a prediction for every class or compiler.
prompts: Where are the two hidden copy constructors in the before expression?
Would getters returning const references change the conclusion?
Why does call frequency determine whether this source-level cleanup matters?
